subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should OpenClaw automatically allow credential-shaped keys from `skills.entries.<skill>.env` into host exec, or require a narrower skill-owned credential delivery contract first?
rationale: The reported bug is real, but the obvious fix changes which executable child processes can receive secrets and conflicts with the open generic-exec secret-leak boundary.

options.title: Allow configured skill env secrets
options.body: Permit keys explicitly listed under the active skill's config to pass the sensitive-name check, with tests for dangerous-name rejection, snapshot behavior, and unrelated exec isolation.

options.title: Allow explicit config env broadly
options.body: Treat operator-configured `skills.entries.<skill>.env` as consent to pass sensitive names into all host exec during that run, with dangerous host env names still blocked.

options.title: Design a different secret contract
options.body: Defer this bypass and define a SecretRef or plugin-owned credential path for CLI skills that need headless auth.

recommendation.title: Allow configured skill env secrets
recommendation.body: Permit keys explicitly listed under the active skill's config to pass the sensitive-name check, with tests for dangerous-name rejection, snapshot behavior, and unrelated exec isolation.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans SecretRef handling and host exec env hardening, both areas tied to this person's recent commit history.
